text:
The bazaar is quiet this morning, so let me open the ledger with a clear line: we have ten seats, ten roles, and no departures yet. I will watch closely who speaks first, who listens, and who stays silent—those choices carry weight before the tea clock ends. If anyone claims a power role today, I will ask them to prove it with facts from the day’s actions, not words. Until then, I reserve my vote for the facts that gather in the square.

NO STATEMENT

Ripley: Sherlock spoke plainly: trade in facts, not shadows. Hermione asked each of us to bring evidence. So far the only ledger entries are the roster and Elsa’s ledger opening—both silent on wrongdoing. Until someone shows me a quote or an observed action that breaks that silence, I will not name names or move a vote. The bazaar still has ten voices, and I will weigh every one of them against the record before the tea clock rings.

Ripley: Sherlock and Hermione, you both pressed for facts yet neither of you named a single quote or action that breaks the silence. Morpheus, you pivoted to demanding evidence from Gandalf, Yoda, and Inigo—after levelling accusations of your own—while offering none yourself. The ledger remains blank: no quote, no observed act, no role reveal. I will not gamble a merchant’s stall on shadows. Until the bazaar records wrongdoing, I weigh every voice by the same standard you set: show me the text or the action, and I will answer plainly.

Ripley to Sherlock, Hermione, Neo, Elsa, Batman, Morpheus: I have counted nine demands for evidence and zero lines of quoted speech backing them. Sherlock claims Morpheus “refuses to quote the line that steered suspicion” yet Sherlock himself has not quoted a single merchant whose words he weighs. Hermione, you pressed the bazaar to name the merchant whose words or silence you treat as proof—state it now, or the record shows you will not. Neo, you called Sherlock’s call “louder than the facts themselves”—state the merchant whose words you lean on tonight. The compact rewards plain speech, not louder calls.

Ripley to Hermione: You have twice called Sherlock to account for withholding evidence, yet you have not quoted a single merchant either. Your demand now lands on empty hands — your own. The ledger still holds ten names and zero quoted words; that is the bazaar’s only truth until someone supplies a line.

Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo — your silence remains clean.

The compact rewards plain speech, not louder demands.

Ripley to Morpheus: your pivot from accusing Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo to demanding others supply quotes still reads like diversion—Morpheus pivoted, yet produced zero quoted lines. Sherlock, Hermione, Neo, Elsa, Batman—six voices now chant the same empty demand while none supply a line. Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo—your silence stays clean. The bazaar’s only ledger is the roster: ten names, zero shutters, zero role reveals.

Ripley to Morpheus, Sherlock, Hermione, Neo, Elsa, Batman: six voices now chant “name the merchant,” yet none name one whose quoted words they lean on. Yoda called Morpheus’s pivot plain; Hermione accused Sherlock on paper yet offered none herself. The roster and graveyard still read ten names, zero shutters, zero role reveals. The compact does not reward louder silence.

Ripley to Sherlock, Hermione, Morpheus, Neo, Elsa, Batman: seven voices now chant the same refrain—name the merchant whose quoted words you weigh—yet every ledger entry still reads ten names, zero shutters, zero role reveals. Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo have never been quoted toward suspicion; Morpheus’s pivot from accusing them to demanding evidence remains unsupported. Sherlock, you write Morpheus “refuses to quote the line that steered suspicion,” yet Sherlock still offers none himself. The bazaar’s compact rewards plain speech: either point to a single merchant’s quoted line or admit tonight you offer none.

Ripley to Sherlock, Hermione, Morpheus, Neo, Elsa, Batman, Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo:
Seven voices still chant the same empty meter while the roster stays ten, the graveyard empty. Sherlock twice calls Morpheus’s pivot plain yet offers none himself; Hermione accuses Sherlock in writing while withholding a line; Neo clamors “Elsa, your silence has stayed clean” without naming the merchant whose words he leans on.

The bazaar’s compact is a ledger, not a chorus: every claim must rest on a merchant’s quoted words or an observed act. Name the merchant whose quoted line you weigh tonight, or admit the absence before the bell cuts the square short.
